definitions.explanation: A railway line with two parallel tracks, so that trains in each direction have their own track and need not wait for one another at passing points. Lines with four tracks are called {複々線|ふくふくせん}.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{路線|ろせん}→路線：11341_rosen⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{複線|ふくせん}だ。
⟦{来年|らいねん}→来年：00745_rainen⟧、⟦{単線|たんせん}→単線：33254_tansen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{区間|くかん}→区間：18759_kukan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{複線化|ふくせんか}⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Next year the single-track section will be double-tracked.

examples.japanese: {複線|ふくせん}になって⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{列車|れっしゃ}→列車：01670_ressha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{本数|ほんすう}→本数：13154_honsuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}え→増える：01183_fueru⟧、⟦{待|ま}ち{時間|じかん}→待ち時間：09621_machijikan⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{短|みじか}く→短い：00510_mijikai⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: Since the line became double-track, there are more trains and shorter waits.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {複線化|ふくせんか}: double-tracking (of a line)
- {複線区間|ふくせんくかん}: a double-track section
- {複々線|ふくふくせん}: a quadruple-track line

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{単線|たんせん}→単線：33254_tansen⟧: single track; the opposite

WATCH OUT:
⟦{伏線|ふくせん}→伏線：10902_fukusen⟧ (foreshadowing in a story) has the same reading but is a different word.
